title: RWB-S9-E7015-APP: the contract end has no operation, the recall has no event, "open" has no definition, the partner service level sits on no PRM rule row and the case-side re-selection has no published boundary
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7015-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E7-015; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.12 and Requirements served; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-45; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 partner, partner_instruction, LOV-PANEL and LOV-INSTR-STATUS; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-PRM-11 and FEAT-PRM-12; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S9-001 and REQ-S9-006
description: (1) The Ownership Map gives S9 six REST operations and none of them ends a partner contract: GET /partners, GET /partner/instructions, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results. The act therefore has no published entry point, the story carries it as a Temporal command on InstructionWorkflow, and the effect is read through the two GET operations. (2) The service owns exactly two events, EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted, and both describe the issue of an instruction and the result the partner records; no event carries a contract end or a recall, so the recall is announced to nobody on Kafka. (3) The word "open" is not defined for an instruction: LOV-INSTR-STATUS carries SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and RECALLED and no source says which of them a recall enumerates. (4) No PRM rule set exists in the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: the domains are R-RES, R-SET, R-DIL, R-GUA, R-LIT, R-DIS, R-DS, R-WO, R-DEV and R-UNI, and the exit is carried by the UNIVERSAL row R-UNI-26 with R-UNI-45, so no partner service level exists on a rule row of its own. (5) The case-side re-selection has no published workflow, activity or operation name, and R-UNI-45's to_state ROUTE_D6_REOPEN is a case route state, so the command is a placeholder. (6) The plan gives H = RWB-S9-E7015-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the path commands rwb-case and loads a rule package of rwb-decision. (7) The context pack gives S9 the table partner_user and TSD S9 T3.1 gives it no field list. (8) The legacy Screen and states table names SCR-35 Placement and allocation and SCR-34 Partner list, both of which carry no contract-end state.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.12.1 to A2.12.4.3 (objective, the placements-by-scorecard metric with DL22, three flow steps, VR-S9-012-1 and BR-S9-012, the eight field-catalog rows, the Partner and agency manager primary with the Head of Litigation and the Head of Asset Liquidity as also using, AC-S9-012-01 and the two exception criteria); TSD S9 T3.1 (partner DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 and partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016), T3.2 (LOV-INSTR-STATUS with RECALLED, LOV-PANEL with EXITED), T3.3 (two relationships, both out of partner_instruction), T4 (no state machine of its own), T5.2, T5.3 (InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted published) and T6.1 (RW-AGENCYMG CRUDA, RW-HEADLIT and RW-HEADASL RA, PT roles RU); TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (the six operations, none of which ends a contract); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-45; LDM v8 partner and partner_instruction; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; context pack S9 ownership rows (three tables, six operations, two events, no job, one workflow), service row (wave 4) and Architecture v5 slide 12 (Temporal for a step in another service) and slide 8 (partner gateway in the DMZ); legacy RWB-E7-015 Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks and Data.
area: API contract, events, business rules, data model, workflow boundary
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case owner, the rwb-decision rule owner and the center of excellence
proposed: Publish an operation for the contract end on /api/recovery/partner/v1, or confirm that the act stays a workflow command driven by the panel maintenance of FEAT-PRM-01; decide whether a recall publishes an event of its own or is read from the instruction status; define "open" for an instruction; publish the case-side re-selection command with its name and its answer; decide whether a PRM rule set and a partner service level row are authored in rwb-decision; publish the field list of partner_user. Until then the story commands the workflow, reads the effect through the two GET operations, publishes nothing and carries the placeholders.

title: RWB-S9-E7015-CON: the contract-end act, the definition of "open", the case command name, the refusal code of a recalled instruction and the partner service level have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7015-CON; context pack S9 rwb-partner; legacy RWB-E7-015; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.12.2 to A2.12.4.3 and Screens; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-45; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 partner_instruction and LOV-INSTR-STATUS; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S9-001 and REQ-S9-006
description: (1) No source publishes an operation that ends a partner contract, so the baseline declares two reads and records the act as a placeholder with no entry point. (2) No column of partner or partner_instruction carries a recall or a re-selection: TSD S9 T3.1 gives seven partner fields and nine instruction fields, and the recall can only be the status RECALLED and the exit the panel status EXITED, so the two elements stay unchanged and the baseline declares no column. (3) The definition of an open instruction has no source, so the command element declares the three statuses SENT, ACCEPTED and IN_PROGRESS with the placeholder. (4) The case-side re-selection command has no published name and no published answer shape, so the commanded element carries the placeholder and the boundary is declared as Temporal. (5) The refusal code for a result submitted on a recalled instruction is unpublished: the baseline fixes the condition and declares 409 or 422 non-committally. (6) No PRM rule set exists, so the clock and the escalation are named from the UNIVERSAL rows R-UNI-26 and R-UNI-30 and the partner service level has no row of its own. (7) The plan's C row is empty although the path commands rwb-case, and DP-07 and DP-09 are not in the pattern set although the lists are read at a version and the service owns a topic. (8) The context pack gives S9 the table partner_user with no field list in TSD S9 T3.1.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.12.2 (integration point Partner portal, prerequisite FEAT-PRM-11), A2.12.3.1 (VR-S9-012-1 and BR-S9-012), A2.12.3.2 (the eight field-catalog rows), A2.12.3.3 (Partner and agency manager primary; Head of Litigation and Head of Asset Liquidity also using), A2.12.4.1 and A2.12.4.3 (AC-S9-012-01 and the two exception criteria), A2.12.4.4 (no background event) and Screens (SCR-34, SCR-35); TSD S9 T2 (write the decision log entry before any change), T3.0 (standard record columns), T3.1 and T3.2 (the two elements and the four lists), T3.3 (relationships to recovery_case and partner), T5.2 and T5.3 (published interfaces, InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted), T6.1 (the role matrix) and T-A.1 and T-A.2 (the six operations and their error sets); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-45; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; context pack S9 ownership rows (three tables, six operations, two events, no job, one workflow); legacy RWB-E7-015 Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks and Validation and messages.
area: API contract, data model, access, reference data, events
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case owner, the rwb-decision rule owner, the rwb-access owner and the platform library owner
proposed: Publish the contract-end operation or confirm the workflow command; define "open" for an instruction; publish the case-side re-selection command with its answer; settle the refusal code of a result on a recalled instruction in the published contract; author a PRM rule row for the partner service level or confirm that R-UNI-26 carries it; confirm the engagement of partner_user. Until then the baseline declares the two reads, the unchanged elements, the commanded element and the entry with the placeholders and the three absences.
